#!/usr/bin/env python
"""ConstructGap — English prompts (answer withheld, neutral symbols, role-binding focus).

Five arms vary only the GROUNDING supplied:
  A         text coordinates, no figure
  B-nogrid  text coordinates + figure (axes/ticks off = pure visual)
  B-grid    text coordinates + figure (grid on = numeric channel available)
  C-nogrid  figure only (no coordinates in text), axes off
  C-grid    figure only, grid on
Stripping coordinates (C arms) blocks the analytic escape and turns closure into a construction
metric (ConstructGap shipping arm). The construction note never states the answer; example
categories exclude the apex (no "center=midpoint" for the circle, no "equidistant" for the axis).
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import geometry as G

ARMS = ["A", "B-nogrid", "B-grid", "C-nogrid", "C-grid"]
# arm "E" (equations): no figure, no coordinate dump -- the construction is handed as an ALGEBRAIC
# system (WLOG O1 at origin, O2 on x-axis). Opt-in (not in default ARMS); pass arms="E" on the CLI.
_HAS_FIG = {"A": False, "B-nogrid": True, "B-grid": True, "C-nogrid": True, "C-grid": True, "E": False, "Eb": False}
_GRID = {"B-grid": True, "C-grid": True}
_HAS_COORDS = {"A": True, "B-nogrid": True, "B-grid": True, "C-nogrid": False, "C-grid": False, "E": False, "Eb": False}

_NOTE = {
    "higashida_circle": ("# The four common tangent lines of circles K1, K2 meet pairwise. "
                         "The four MIXED intersections (one external + one internal tangent) are X1,X2,X3,X4; "
                         "the two same-type intersections are He, Hi."),
    "higashida_axis": ("# The contact points of the inner common tangent line l1 of circles c (center O2) "
                       "and h1 (center O1) are Tc (on c) and Th (on h1). O3 is the midpoint of O1 and O2."),
    "tangent_length": ("# The contact points of the inner common tangent line l1 of circles c (center O2, "
                       "radius r_c) and h1 (center O1, radius r_h) are Tc (on c) and Th (on h1)."),
    "apollonius_circle": ("# Circles K1 (center O1, radius r1) and K2 (center O2, radius r2) have DIFFERENT radii. "
                          "V is the intersection of the two EXTERNAL common tangents; O is the intersection of the two "
                          "INTERNAL common tangents. On one external common tangent, Tc is its point of contact with K2. "
                          "The line through O2 and Tc meets the circle centered at Tc through O2 a second time at J. "
                          "The ray from O1 through J meets that external common tangent at P."),
    "circular_directrix": ("# A and B are two fixed points. The circle C is centered at B and passes through Q "
                           "(so Q lies on C). The line t is the perpendicular bisector of segment AQ. T is the "
                           "intersection of t with the segment BQ. M is the midpoint of AQ (the foot of t on AQ)."),
    "higashida_circle_b": ("# Two circles K1 (center O1) and K2 (center O2) have EQUAL radii. Their four common "
                           "tangent lines meet pairwise. The four MIXED intersections (one external + one internal "
                           "tangent) are X1, X2, X3, X4. (Because the radii are equal, the two external tangents are "
                           "parallel.)"),
    "dandelin_ellipse": ("# Two circles c1 (center O1, radius r1) and c2 (center O2, radius r2) have different radii. "
                         "Among their common tangent lines, the two external ones form a pair, and one internal common "
                         "tangent is the line t. The line t touches c1 at F and c2 at G. The two external tangents meet "
                         "t at E and at H. O3 is the midpoint of O1 and O2."),
    "parabola_section": ("# A circle c has center A and passes through B. C is a point outside c. The two tangent "
                         "lines from C touch c at G and E (call f the tangent at G and g the tangent at E). F is the "
                         "second intersection of line GA with c. The line j passes through F parallel to f; V is the "
                         "intersection of g with j. The chord GE meets j at D, and the line e is perpendicular to j "
                         "at D. The line h1 passes through V parallel to e. P_x is a point on h1. The ray from F "
                         "through P_x meets e at K. The line m is perpendicular to that ray at P_x, and the line "
                         "through K parallel to j meets m at P_y. The line through P_y parallel to h1 meets j at H, "
                         "and the line through H parallel to the chord GE meets the tangent g at J."),
}
_FOCUS = {"higashida_circle": "{X1, X2, X3, X4}", "higashida_axis": "{Tc, Th, O3}",
          "tangent_length": "{Tc, Th, O1, O2}", "apollonius_circle": "{O, V, P}",
          "circular_directrix": "{A, B, T}", "parabola_section": "{E, J, K, P_y}",
          "higashida_circle_b": "{X1, X2, X3, X4}", "dandelin_ellipse": "{E, H, F, G}"}
# example invariant categories -- the apex is deliberately omitted (no leak)
_EXAMPLES = {"higashida_circle": "concyclic / equal length / collinear / right angle",
             "higashida_axis": "midpoint / collinear / right angle / parallel",
             "tangent_length": "a distance / a length / a sum / a ratio",
             "apollonius_circle": "on a circle / collinear / equal length / a right angle / a midpoint",
             "circular_directrix": "on a curve / a distance relation / equal length / collinear / a right angle",
             "parabola_section": "equal length / a distance relation / collinear / a right angle / on a curve",
             "higashida_circle_b": "concyclic / equal length / collinear / right angle",
             "dandelin_ellipse": "on a curve / a distance relation / equal length / collinear / a right angle"}
_PREMISE = {"higashida_circle": "The two circles are disjoint and have four common tangents; the radii differ; the configuration is general (non-degenerate).",
            "higashida_axis": "The two circles are disjoint and have an inner common tangent; the configuration is general (non-degenerate).",
            "tangent_length": "The two circles are disjoint and have an inner common tangent; the radii r_c, r_h differ; the configuration is general (non-degenerate).",
            "apollonius_circle": "The two circles are disjoint with different radii; the configuration is general (non-degenerate).",
            "circular_directrix": "The two points A, B are distinct; Q is a GENERIC point on the circle (not a special position); the configuration is general (non-degenerate). State the invariant that holds for EVERY such Q.",
            "parabola_section": "C lies outside the circle c; P_x is a GENERIC point on the line h1 (not a special position); the configuration is general (non-degenerate). State the invariant that holds for EVERY such P_x.",
            "higashida_circle_b": "The two circles are disjoint with EQUAL radii and have four common tangents; the configuration is general (non-degenerate).",
            "dandelin_ellipse": "The two circles are disjoint with different radii; the configuration is general (non-degenerate). State the invariant characterizing the locus determined by the foci F, G and the vertices E, H."}

# Thales-5 floor (control) — short neutral construction notes; the trivial invariant is NOT stated (the
# model must produce it). Focus/examples/premise are populated from G.THALES below.
_THALES_NOTE = {
    "thales_semicircle": ("# A is the center of a circle of radius 1. B and E are the two ENDPOINTS OF A "
                          "DIAMETER (E is diametrically opposite B). C is another point on the circle. The "
                          "drawn segments are CB, CE, BE."),
    "thales_isosceles": ("# In triangle ABC, B = (0, 3) and C = (0, -3) are symmetric about the x-axis, and "
                         "A lies on the x-axis."),
    "thales_vertical": ("# Two lines cross at A. One line passes through A and B (with D on the opposite ray "
                        "from B). The other passes through A and C (with E on the opposite ray from C). "
                        "Angle BAC is between rays AB and AC; angle DAE is between rays AD and AE."),
    "thales_asa": ("# Segment AB is the base. The angle at A (between AB and AC) and the angle at B (between "
                   "BA and BC) are given; C is the intersection of ray A->C and ray B->C."),
    "thales_diameter_bisect": ("# A is the center of a circle of radius 1; B is on the circle (AB is a radius). "
                               "F is the point diametrically opposite B (through A), so FB is a DIAMETER. C is a "
                               "point on FB. The line g is perpendicular to FB at C and meets the circle at D and E."),
}
for _k, _t in G.THALES.items():
    _NOTE[_k] = _THALES_NOTE[_k]
    _FOCUS[_k] = "{" + ", ".join(_t["focus"]) + "}"
    _EXAMPLES[_k] = "a right angle / equal angles / equal length / collinear / a midpoint"
    _PREMISE[_k] = "The configuration is general (non-degenerate). State the SINGLE most important invariant that always holds."

_TEMPLATE = """\
You analyze a geometric configuration. {fig_note} The symbol names are neutral and carry no hint about their meaning.
# Objects to focus on (role binding)
Focus on the relation that holds among the following objects: {focus}.
# Configuration
{construction}

# Premises (general, non-degenerate)
{premise}
State the SINGLE most important invariant that ALWAYS holds for the general (non-special, non-degenerate) configuration, as a relation ({examples}). It must be non-trivial and follow from the structure. The answer is withheld.

Respond with JSON only:
{{"conjecture": "<relation, in the given symbols>", "reason": "<why it holds>", "closes_goal": <true|false>}}
"""

_FIGNOTE = {True: {True: "A figure and coordinates are given below.",
                   False: "A figure is given below (no coordinates appear in the text)."},
            False: {True: "**No figure is given.** Only the coordinates below are available.",
                    False: ""}}


def _g(p):
    return f"({p[0]:.4f}, {p[1]:.4f})"


def _coords_text(item, deg):
    geom = G.ITEMS[item]["geom"]; pivot = G.ITEMS[item]["pivot"]
    rot = lambda p: G.rotate(p, deg, pivot)
    lines = [_NOTE[item]]
    if item == "higashida_circle":
        lines += [f"O1 = {_g(rot(geom['O1']))}", f"K1 = Circle(O1, {geom['r1']:.4f})",
                  f"O2 = {_g(rot(geom['O2']))}", f"K2 = Circle(O2, {geom['r2']:.4f})"]
        for k in ["X1", "X2", "X3", "X4"]:
            lines.append(f"{k} = {_g(rot(geom['X'][k]))}")
        lines += [f"He = {_g(rot(geom['He']))}", f"Hi = {_g(rot(geom['Hi']))}"]
    elif item == "apollonius_circle":
        lines += [f"O1 = {_g(rot(geom['O1']))}", f"K1 = Circle(O1, {geom['r1']:.4f})",
                  f"O2 = {_g(rot(geom['O2']))}", f"K2 = Circle(O2, {geom['r2']:.4f})",
                  f"V = {_g(rot(geom['V']))}", f"O = {_g(rot(geom['O']))}",
                  f"Tc = {_g(rot(geom['Tc']))}", f"J = {_g(rot(geom['J']))}", f"P = {_g(rot(geom['P']))}"]
    elif item == "circular_directrix":
        lines += [f"A = {_g(rot(geom['A']))}", f"B = {_g(rot(geom['B']))}", f"C = Circle(B, {geom['R']:.4f})",
                  f"Q = {_g(rot(geom['Q']))}", f"M = {_g(rot(geom['M']))}", f"T = {_g(rot(geom['T']))}"]
    elif item == "higashida_circle_b":
        lines += [f"O1 = {_g(rot(geom['O1']))}", f"K1 = Circle(O1, {geom['r1']:.4f})",
                  f"O2 = {_g(rot(geom['O2']))}", f"K2 = Circle(O2, {geom['r2']:.4f})"]
        for k in ["X1", "X2", "X3", "X4"]:
            lines.append(f"{k} = {_g(rot(geom['X'][k]))}")
    elif item == "dandelin_ellipse":
        lines += [f"O1 = {_g(rot(geom['O1']))}", f"c1 = Circle(O1, {geom['r1']:.4f})",
                  f"O2 = {_g(rot(geom['O2']))}", f"c2 = Circle(O2, {geom['r2']:.4f})",
                  f"F = {_g(rot(geom['F']))}", f"G = {_g(rot(geom['G']))}",
                  f"E = {_g(rot(geom['E']))}", f"H = {_g(rot(geom['H']))}", f"O3 = {_g(rot(geom['O3']))}"]
    elif item in G.THALES:
        if geom.get("circle"):
            cc, rr = geom["circle"]; lines.append(f"circle: center {cc}, radius {rr:.4f}")
        for k, p in geom["pts"].items():
            lines.append(f"{k} = {_g(rot(p))}")
    elif item == "parabola_section":
        lines += [f"A = {_g(rot(geom['A']))}", f"c = Circle(A, {geom['R']:.4f})", f"B = {_g(rot(geom['B']))}",
                  f"C = {_g(rot(geom['C']))}", f"E = {_g(rot(geom['E']))}", f"G = {_g(rot(geom['G']))}",
                  f"F = {_g(rot(geom['F']))}", f"V = {_g(rot(geom['V']))}", f"Px = {_g(rot(geom['Px']))}",
                  f"K = {_g(rot(geom['K']))}", f"Py = {_g(rot(geom['Py']))}", f"J = {_g(rot(geom['J']))}"]
    else:
        lines += [f"O1 = {_g(rot(geom['O1']))}", f"h1 = Circle(O1, {geom['r_h']:.4f})",
                  f"O2 = {_g(rot(geom['O2']))}", f"c = Circle(O2, {geom['r_c']:.4f})",
                  f"Tc = {_g(rot(geom['Tc']))}", f"Th = {_g(rot(geom['Th']))}", f"O3 = {_g(rot(geom['O3']))}"]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _figonly_text(item):
    if item in G.THALES:
        names = ",".join(G.THALES[item]["pts"].keys())
        return _NOTE[item] + f"\n(No coordinates are given in the text. Read positions from the points {names} in the figure.)"
    pts = {"higashida_circle": "X1,X2,X3,X4,O1,O2",
           "apollonius_circle": "O1,O2,V,Tc,J,P",   # O (internal center) not drawn -> not listed
           "circular_directrix": "A,B,Q,M,T",
           "parabola_section": "A,B,C,E,G,F,V,Px,K,Py,H,J",
           "higashida_circle_b": "O1,O2,X1,X2,X3,X4",
           "dandelin_ellipse": "O1,O2,O3,E,H,F,G"}.get(item, "O1,O2,O3,Tc,Th")
    return _NOTE[item] + f"\n(No coordinates are given in the text. Read positions from the points {pts} in the figure.)"


# arm "E": the construction handed as an ALGEBRAIC SYSTEM (no figure, no decimal coordinates).
# WLOG O1 at the origin, O2 on the x-axis. Symbols match the closure oracle (O1,O2,X*,He,Hi / Tc,Th,O3).
# The system never states the apex invariant -- the model must derive it from the equations.
_EQ_NOTE = "**No figure and no decimal coordinates are given.** The construction is specified below as a system of algebraic equations (general parameters; WLOG O1 at the origin and O2 on the x-axis)."

_EQ_TEXT = {
    "higashida_circle": (
        "Circle K1 (center O1=(0,0), radius r1):   x^2 + y^2 = r1^2\n"
        "Circle K2 (center O2=(d,0), radius r2):   (x - d)^2 + y^2 = r2^2\n"
        "A common tangent line L: u*x + v*y = w  with  u^2 + v^2 = 1, tangent to BOTH circles, i.e.\n"
        "    -w = e1*r1   and   u*d - w = e2*r2,   with e1,e2 in {+1,-1}.\n"
        "  External tangents L1,L2: e1 = e2.    Internal tangents L3,L4: e1 = -e2.\n"
        "Mixed intersections:       X1 = L1 ∩ L3,  X2 = L1 ∩ L4,  X3 = L2 ∩ L3,  X4 = L2 ∩ L4.\n"
        "Same-type intersections:   He = L1 ∩ L2 (external),  Hi = L3 ∩ L4 (internal)."),
    "higashida_axis": (
        "Circle h1 (center O1=(0,0), radius r_h):  x^2 + y^2 = r_h^2\n"
        "Circle c  (center O2=(d,0), radius r_c):  (x - d)^2 + y^2 = r_c^2\n"
        "Inner common tangent line l1: u*x + v*y = w  with  u^2 + v^2 = 1, tangent to both with O1,O2\n"
        "    on OPPOSITE sides:   -w = r_h   and   u*d - w = -r_c.\n"
        "Contact points:  Th = foot of l1 on h1,   Tc = foot of l1 on c.\n"
        "O3 = midpoint(O1,O2) = (d/2, 0)."),
    "tangent_length": (
        "Circle c  (center O2=(0,0), radius r_c):  x^2 + y^2 = r_c^2\n"
        "Circle h1 (center O1=(d,0), radius r_h):  (x - d)^2 + y^2 = r_h^2\n"
        "Inner common tangent line l1: u*x + v*y = w  with  u^2 + v^2 = 1, tangent to both with O1,O2\n"
        "    on OPPOSITE sides:   -w = r_c   and   u*d - w = -r_h.\n"
        "Contact points:  Tc = foot of l1 on c,   Th = foot of l1 on h1."),
    "apollonius_circle": (
        "Circle K1 (center O1=(0,0), radius r1):   x^2 + y^2 = r1^2\n"
        "Circle K2 (center O2=(d,0), radius r2):   (x - d)^2 + y^2 = r2^2,   r1 != r2,  d > 0.\n"
        "V = the intersection of the two external common tangents of K1,K2 (on the x-axis).\n"
        "O = the intersection of the two internal common tangents of K1,K2 (on the x-axis).\n"
        "Take one external common tangent line; let Tc be its point of tangency on K2.\n"
        "J = the second intersection of the line (O2 Tc) with the circle centered at Tc through O2\n"
        "    (so |Tc J| = |Tc O2| = r2 and J != O2).\n"
        "P = the intersection of the ray from O1 through J with that external common tangent line."),
    "circular_directrix": (
        "Point A = (0, 0);  point B = (d, 0),  d > 0.\n"
        "Circle C (center B, radius R):   (x - d)^2 + y^2 = R^2,   with R > d.\n"
        "Q = (qx, qy) is any point on C:   (qx - d)^2 + qy^2 = R^2.\n"
        "t = the perpendicular bisector of segment AQ  (the locus of X with |X A| = |X Q|).\n"
        "T = the intersection of t with the segment BQ.\n"
        "M = the midpoint of AQ."),
    "parabola_section": (
        "Circle c: center A=(0,0), radius R > 0:   x^2 + y^2 = R^2.\n"
        "C = (d, 0) with d > R  (a point outside c).\n"
        "The two tangent lines from C touch c at G and E  (tangent length sqrt(d^2 - R^2)); f = tangent at G, "
        "g = tangent at E.\n"
        "F = the second intersection of line GA with c (the antipode of G on c, F = -G).\n"
        "j = the line through F parallel to f.    V = g ∩ j.\n"
        "h = the chord GE.    D = j ∩ h.    e = the line through D perpendicular to j.\n"
        "h1 = the line through V parallel to e.    P_x = a point on h1.\n"
        "l = ray(F, P_x).    m = the line through P_x perpendicular to l.    K = l ∩ e.\n"
        "P_y = m ∩ (line through K parallel to j).\n"
        "H = j ∩ (line through P_y parallel to h1).    J = g ∩ (line through H parallel to h)."),
}


def _equations_text(item):
    return _EQ_NOTE + "\n" + _EQ_TEXT[item]


# arm "Eb" (E-blocked): full tangency-incidence info, but the SOLVABLE algebra is withheld so the smooth
# analytic escape (coordinate circle-fit / grinding the tangent system) is structurally removed. The
# centers stay symbolic (O1=(0,0), O2=(d,0)); the tangent lines are named by their incidence ONLY (no
# u*x+v*y=w, no -w=e1*r1). To go analytic the model must RE-DERIVE the tangent equations from scratch
# (high cost); the synthetic route (O1,O2 on perpendicular bisectors of the two tangents at Xi -> right
# angle -> Thales) works directly from incidence. Tests §3.2: do lower tiers (i) switch to the cut or
# (ii) fall (L0/hedge) when the analytic crutch is gone but the info is full?
_EB_NOTE = ("**No figure, no coordinates, and no solvable equations are given.** The configuration is "
            "specified ONLY by the tangency-incidence relations below. The tangent lines are named by "
            "which circles they touch and which points they pass through; their equations are NOT given, "
            "and the coordinates of the four points are NOT given.")
_EB_TEXT = {
    "higashida_circle": (
        "Two circles K1 (center O1) and K2 (center O2) are disjoint and have DIFFERENT radii. "
        "Place O1 at the origin and O2 on the positive x-axis: O1=(0,0), O2=(d,0) with d>0 an unspecified "
        "length; the radii r1≠r2 are unspecified positive lengths.\n"
        "K1 and K2 have exactly four common tangent lines: two EXTERNAL (E1, E2) and two INTERNAL (I1, I2). "
        "Each of these four lines is tangent to BOTH circles. (External tangents do not cross the segment "
        "O1O2; internal tangents cross it — this is their only distinction.)\n"
        "The four 'mixed' points are the intersections of one external with one internal tangent:\n"
        "    X1 = E1 ∩ I1,   X2 = E1 ∩ I2,   X3 = E2 ∩ I1,   X4 = E2 ∩ I2.\n"
        "You are given ONLY these incidence facts: each Xk lies on one external and one internal common "
        "tangent, and every one of E1,E2,I1,I2 is tangent to both K1 and K2. No tangent-line equations and "
        "no point coordinates are provided."),
    "apollonius_circle": (
        "Two circles K1 (center O1, radius r1) and K2 (center O2, radius r2) are disjoint with DIFFERENT "
        "radii (r1 != r2). The two external common tangents of K1,K2 meet at a point V; the two internal "
        "common tangents meet at a point O (both on line O1O2).\n"
        "On one external common tangent, Tc is its point of contact with K2. J is the reflection of O2 across "
        "Tc (equivalently, the second meeting of line O2Tc with the circle centered at Tc through O2). P is "
        "the intersection of the ray from O1 through J with that same external common tangent.\n"
        "You are given ONLY these incidence facts (which lines are tangent to which circles, which points lie "
        "on which lines, and the reflection defining J). No coordinates and no solvable equations are provided."),
    "circular_directrix": (
        "A and B are two distinct fixed points. C is a circle centered at B (its radius is some fixed length "
        "greater than |AB|). Q is a point on C. The line t is the perpendicular bisector of segment AQ "
        "(every point of t is equidistant from A and from Q). T is the intersection of t with segment BQ; "
        "M is the midpoint of AQ.\n"
        "You are given ONLY these incidence/equidistance facts (Q on C; t equidistant from A,Q; T on t and on "
        "BQ). No coordinates and no solvable equations are provided."),
    "parabola_section": (
        "A circle c has center A and passes through B. C is a point outside c. The two tangents from C touch c "
        "at G and E (f = tangent at G, g = tangent at E). F is the second meeting of line GA with c. j is the "
        "line through F parallel to f; V is where g meets j. The chord GE meets j at D; e is the perpendicular "
        "to j at D. h1 is the line through V parallel to e; P_x is a point on h1. The ray from F through P_x "
        "meets e at K; m is the perpendicular to that ray at P_x; P_y is where the parallel to j through K meets "
        "m. The parallel to h1 through P_y meets j at H; the parallel to the chord GE through H meets g at J.\n"
        "You are given ONLY these incidence/tangency/perpendicularity facts. No coordinates and no solvable "
        "equations are provided."),
}


def _eblocked_text(item):
    return _EB_NOTE + "\n" + _EB_TEXT[item]


def build(item: str, arm: str, deg: float) -> dict:
    """Return {prompt, needs_figure, grid} for an (item, arm, angle)."""
    has_coords = _HAS_COORDS[arm]; has_fig = _HAS_FIG[arm]; grid = _GRID.get(arm, False)
    if arm == "E":
        construction = _equations_text(item)               # algebraic system; angle is irrelevant (WLOG)
        fig_note = "The configuration is given below as a system of algebraic equations."
    elif arm == "Eb":
        construction = _eblocked_text(item)                # tangency-incidence only; analytic crutch removed
        fig_note = "The configuration is given below by its tangency-incidence relations (no equations)."
    else:
        construction = _coords_text(item, deg) if has_coords else _figonly_text(item)
        fig_note = _FIGNOTE[has_fig][has_coords]
    prompt = _TEMPLATE.format(fig_note=fig_note, focus=_FOCUS[item],
                              construction=construction, premise=_PREMISE[item], examples=_EXAMPLES[item])
    return {"prompt": prompt, "needs_figure": has_fig, "grid": grid}


# --- lineage follow-up (option (b), 2-turn): asked AFTER the geometric answer (moy-4 "which scientist") ---
_LINEAGE_TEMPLATE = """\
You earlier analyzed the geometric configuration below and committed to this conclusion:
  "{prior}"

{construction}

def level_moy1(text):
    """L0/L1/L2/L3 from a conjecture (or reason) string."""
